items.title: Frank Tate interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: Felix Grant, the disc jockey, used to talk about him

ctx.x: Yeah but okay, the idea that the music itself was enough. Like I don’t need to try to entertain you.

Yeah. Yeah, yeah yeah. Dizzy knew better. Dizzy always knew better. He knew where the money was and that was in sending people home happy. If they go home happy they’ll come back. Al Haig never — I worked with him for a couple of weeks. He’d finish a tune by like [mumbles] almost an effort to keep people from applauding. It’s like there was a wall up between, well he was an unusual guy. Brilliant talent. But didn’t know the first thing about entertaining. And Zoot, who [mumbles] good night, thank you. People…

him, he’d say “he’s so much fun to watch.” He was also one of the funniest people on the planet without ever trying. Nothing was ever strained with him he was genuinely interesting, and boy did he have a hard — he had people that would lie down in front of a truck for him. His fans. Oh yeah. And people still talk more about Zoot than anybody, and people miss him. I miss Zoot Sims more than anybody than I can think of. I think about him all the time because of his personality. And he was loaded a lot of the time.…
